posts.text: George Washington died at age 67 from “quincy”, an old name for a peritonsillar abscess. You’ve probably never heard of quincy because almost no one in the US dies from this disease. That’s because it’s essentially the consequence of a bad case of strep throat that goes untreated. It rarely happens now because we have oral antibiotics to treat strep throat infections and surgical drainage and IV antibiotics to treat advanced conditions such as that which killed Pres Washington. But if people started dying from strep throat now because they were being told falsely that antibiotics were harmful, or in kids that they caused autism, there would be a massive federal public health pushback. Right? But that’s exactly what’s occurring currently with measles. People are dying from an ancient disease that can be readily and safely prevented, but the federal government is largely silent.
